# 12-Week General Strength Programme
## Client Profile: 42M, Desk Worker, Post-Disc Herniation (L4-L5, Asymptomatic)

---

## Programme Overview

This 12-week programme prioritises spinal stability and neutral-spine strength while building general fitness. The client will train four days per week across three phases: **Foundation (Weeks 1–4)**, **Development (Weeks 5–8)**, and **Consolidation (Weeks 9–12)**. All exercises avoid loaded spinal flexion and heavy axial loading through a flexed spine. Emphasis falls on anti-rotation, anti-extension, and anti-lateral flexion work, plus posterior-chain and core stability.

---

## Key Principles

1. **Neutral spine maintained throughout** – no loaded forward bending or heavy deadlifts from the floor
2. **Progressive loading** – gradual increases in weight and complexity, not volume
3. **Posterior chain emphasis** – glutes, hamstrings, and upper back to counteract desk posture
4. **Core stability over core flexion** – planks, Pallof presses, bird dogs, not crunches
5. **Movement quality first** – form checked before load increases
6. **Recovery prioritised** – adequate sleep, hydration, and mobility work

---

## Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

**Objective:** Establish movement patterns, build baseline strength, assess tolerance, reinforce spinal stability.

**Training Split:** 4 days per week
- **Day 1:** Lower Body (Squat-Dominant)
- **Day 2:** Upper Body Push
- **Day 3:** Lower Body (Hinge-Dominant)
- **Day 4:** Upper Body Pull + Core

**Rest Days:** Minimum 48 hours between lower-body sessions; at least one full rest day per week.

---

### **Week 1**

#### **Day 1: Lower Body (Squat-Dominant)**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Notes |
|----------|------|------|-------|
| Goblet Squat | 3 | 10 | Weight held at chest; elbows inside knees; neutral spine |
| Leg Press (machine) | 3 | 12 | Back and head supported; full range without lumbar rounding |
| Bulgarian Split Squat | 3 | 8 each | Rear foot elevated; front knee tracking over toe |
| Leg Curl (machine) | 3 | 12 | Controlled tempo; 2-second hold at top |
| Glute Bridge (bodyweight) | 3 | 15 | Squeeze glutes hard; neutral spine; no hyperextension |
| Dead Bug | 2 | 10 each side | Slow, controlled; maintain neutral lumbar spine |

**Rest between sets:** 60–90 seconds for compound lifts; 45 seconds for isolation.

---

#### **Day 2: Upper Body Push**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Notes |
|----------|------|------|-------|
| Dumbbell Bench Press | 3 | 10 | Neutral grip; scapulae retracted; controlled descent |
| Incline Dumbbell Press | 3 | 10 | 30–45° incline; same form cues |
| Machine Chest Fly | 3 | 12 | Controlled; no heavy stretch at bottom |
| Dumbbell Shoulder Press (seated) | 3 | 10 | Seated to reduce spinal load; neutral spine |
| Lateral Raise | 3 | 12 | Light weight; controlled; no momentum |
| Tricep Rope Pushdown | 3 | 12 | Full range; controlled eccentric |

**Rest between sets:** 60–90 seconds.

---

#### **Day 3: Lower Body (Hinge-Dominant)**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Notes |
|----------|------|------|-------|
| Trap Bar Deadlift (light) | 3 | 8 | Neutral spine; slight knee bend; pull from mid-foot; start light |
| Romanian Deadlift (dumbbell) | 3 | 10 | Slight knee bend; hinge at hips; feel hamstring stretch; no rounding |
| Leg Press | 3 | 12 | Variation from Day 1; different foot position (slightly wider) |
| Leg Extension | 3 | 12 | Quad isolation; controlled |
| Glute-Ham Raise (assisted if needed) | 3 | 8 | Posterior chain; eccentric emphasis |
| Pallof Press (cable) | 3 | 10 each side | Anti-rotation core; tall posture; resist rotation |

**Rest between sets:** 60–90 seconds.

---

#### **Day 4: Upper Body Pull + Core**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Notes |
|----------|------|------|-------|
| Lat Pulldown | 3 | 10 | Chest up; scapular retraction; controlled |
| Seated Row (machine) | 3 | 10 | Chest supported; retract scapulae; neutral spine |
| Single-Arm Dumbbell Row | 3 | 10 each | Neutral spine; no rotation; elbow to hip |
| Face Pull (rope) | 3 | 15 | Rear delt and upper back; high reps; external rotation |
| Barbell Curl | 3 | 10 | Strict form; no spinal extension |
| Plank (forearm) | 3 | 30–45 sec | Neutral spine; glutes engaged; no sagging hips |
| Bird Dog | 2 | 10 each side | Slow, controlled; opposite arm and leg |

**Rest between sets:** 60 seconds for compound; 45 seconds for isolation and core.

---

### **Weeks 2–4: Progression**

Repeat the same structure but progress as follows:

- **Week 2:** Add 1–2 reps to each exercise, or increase weight by 2.5–5 kg on compound lifts if form is solid.
- **Week 3:** Add another 1–2 reps or 2.5–5 kg; introduce tempo work (e.g., 3-second eccentric on key lifts).
- **Week 4:** Deload week – reduce volume by 40% (fewer sets or reps), maintain intensity; focus on movement quality and recovery.

**Example Week 4 adjustment:** Goblet Squat 2 × 10, Leg Press 2 × 12, Bulgarian Split Squat 2 × 8, etc.

---

## Phase 2: Development (Weeks 5–8)

**Objective:** Increase strength and work capacity; introduce more complex movement patterns; build confidence in loaded positions.

**Training Split:** Same 4-day structure, but exercises and loading evolve.

---

### **Week 5**

#### **Day 1: Lower Body (Squat-Dominant)**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Notes |
|----------|------|------|-------|
| Back Squat (light–moderate) | 4 | 6–8 | Introduce barbell; conservative load; perfect form; spotter if available |
| Leg Press | 3 | 10 | Increase load from Phase 1 |
| Bulgarian Split Squat | 3 | 8 each | Add 1–2 kg dumbbells if bodyweight is easy |
| Leg Curl | 3 | 12 | Increase load slightly |
| Single-Leg Glute Bridge | 3 | 10 each | Progress from bilateral; stability challenge |
| Suitcase Carry | 3 | 40 m each side | Anti-lateral flexion; heavy dumbbell; tall posture |

**Rest between sets:** 90–120 seconds for squats; 60–90 seconds for others.

---

#### **Day 2: Upper Body Push**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Notes |
|----------|------|------|-------|
| Barbell Bench Press | 4 | 6–8 | Introduce barbell; conservative load; full ROM |
| Incline Dumbbell Press | 3 | 8–10 | Increase load from Phase 1 |
| Machine Chest Fly | 3 | 12 | Increase load |
| Standing Shoulder Press (dumbbell) | 3 | 8 | Progress from seated; core stability challenge |
| Lateral Raise | 3 | 12 | Increase load |
| Tricep Dip (assisted if needed) | 3 | 8–10 | Bodyweight or machine-assisted; controlled |

---

#### **Day 3: Lower Body (Hinge-Dominant)**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Notes |
|----------|------|------|-------|
| Trap Bar Deadlift | 4 | 6–8 | Increase load from Week 1; maintain neutral spine; video form check |
| Romanian Deadlift (barbell) | 3 | 8 | Progress to barbell; lighter than trap bar; hamstring focus |
| Leg Press (different angle) | 3 | 10 | Vary foot position; different stimulus |

## Nutrition Guidance

- **Protein:** 1.6–2.0 g per kg bodyweight (e.g., 100–130 g for an 80 kg person)
- **Carbohydrate:** 4–6 g per kg bodyweight (320–480 g for 80 kg)
- **Fat:** 0.8–1.2 g per kg bodyweight (64–96 g for 80 kg)

### **Meal Timing**

- **Pre-workout (1–2 hours before):** Carbs + moderate protein (e.g., oats + banana, rice cakes + chicken)
- **Post-workout (within 2 hours):** Protein + carbs (e.g., whey shake + dextrose, chicken + rice)
- **Throughout the day:** Distribute protein evenly across 4–5 meals

### **Hydration**

- Minimum 2.5–3 L water daily; more on training days
- Electrolytes (sodium, potassium) if training in heat or sweating heavily

### **Supplements (Optional)**

- **Whey protein:** Convenient post-workout option

## Recovery & Mobility

### **Sleep**

- Target 7–9 hours per night; consistent bedtime and wake time
- Avoid screens 30–60 minutes before bed
- Cool, dark room

### **Active Recovery Days**

- Light walking (20–30 minutes)
- Yoga or mobility work (15–20 minutes)
- Foam rolling (10 minutes)
- Swimming or cycling (low intensity, 20–30 minutes)

### **Mobility Work (3–4 times per week, 10–15 minutes)**

- **Hip flexor stretch:** Couch stretch, 90/90 position
- **Hamstring stretch:** Lying hamstring, standing forward fold (slight knee bend)
- **Thoracic rotation:** Quadruped T-spine rotation, half-kneeling rotation
- **Glute activation:** Clamshells, fire hydrants, glute bridges
- **Spinal mobility:** Cat-cow, bird dogs, quadruped rocking
- **Shoulder mobility:** Arm circles, band pull-aparts, wall slides

- Quads, hamstrings, glutes, calves, upper back

- Slow, controlled passes; 30–60 seconds per muscle group

## Monitoring & Adjustments

### **Weekly Check-Ins**

- **Form:** Video key lifts (squat, deadlift, bench) weekly; review for deviations
- **Pain:** Any sharp or radiating pain in lower back = stop exercise, assess, modify or regress
- **Soreness:** Mild DOMS (delayed-onset muscle soreness) is normal; severe soreness suggests overload
- **Fatigue:** Rate perceived exertion (RPE) on a scale of 1–10; aim for 7–8 on compound lifts

### **Red Flags (Stop & Reassess)**

- Sharp, shooting pain in lower back or legs
- Numbness or tingling in legs or feet
- Pain that worsens over the session
- Inability to maintain neutral spine under load

### **Adjustments**

- If pain occurs: regress to previous week's volume; reduce load by 10–20%; consider alternative exercise
- If progress stalls: check sleep, nutrition, and stress; deload week; vary exercise selection
- If client feels strong: progress load by 5–10 kg on compound lifts; add reps to isolation exercises

This 12-week programme builds general strength while respecting the client's spinal history. Chronic inflammation can impair recovery, exacerbate joint pain, and slow adaptation to training. A desk worker with a history of disc herniation benefits from an anti-inflammatory dietary approach that reduces systemic inflammation, supports tissue repair, and optimises body composition. This plan combines macronutrient targets with micronutrient density and strategic food choices to create an environment conducive to healing and strength gain.

#### **Refined Carbohydrates**
- White bread, white rice, pastries, sugary cereals, biscuits
- **Why:** High glycemic index; spike blood sugar and insulin; promote inflammation
- **Alternative:** Whole grains, legumes, vegetables

#### **Seed Oils (High Omega-6)**
- Vegetable oil, canola oil, sunflower oil, soybean oil, corn oil
- **Why:** High omega-6 to omega-3 ratio; promote inflammation
- **Alternative:** Olive oil, avocado oil, coconut oil (for high-heat cooking)

#### **Processed & Ultra-Processed Foods**
- Packaged snacks, fast food, deli meats, processed cheese, energy drinks
- **Why:** Trans fats, additives, excess sodium, refined carbs; inflammatory
- **Alternative:** Whole foods prepared at home

#### **Excess Sugar & Sweetened Beverages**
- Soft drinks, fruit juices, energy drinks, desserts, sweets
- **Why:** Fructose promotes liver inflammation; spikes blood sugar
- **Alternative:** Water, tea, whole fruit, dark chocolate

- Beer, spirits, wine
- **Why:** Excess alcohol increases intestinal permeability ("leaky gut"); promotes inflammation
- **Guideline:** ≤2 units per day for men; 3–4 days per week maximum

#### **Trans Fats**
- Margarine, shortening, fried foods, baked goods with "partially hydrogenated oils"
- **Why:** Directly inflammatory; increase LDL and reduce HDL
- **Alternative:** Butter, olive oil, avocado oil

## Updated Programme Overview

This 12-week programme now incorporates **two dedicated cardio sessions per week** alongside the four strength-training days. The cardio is strategically placed to complement strength work without compromising recovery or spinal stability. All sessions maintain the neutral-spine principles established for the strength component.

**Weekly Structure:**

## Cardio Principles for Post-Disc Herniation

### **Why Cardio Matters**

1. **Cardiovascular health:** Improves aerobic capacity and heart health
2. **Recovery enhancement:** Low-intensity cardio promotes blood flow and nutrient delivery
3. **Fat loss support:** Caloric deficit without excessive strength volume reduction
4. **Mental health:** Stress reduction and mood improvement
5. **Spinal stability:** Controlled, low-impact movement reinforces core engagement

### **Key Constraints**

- **Avoid high-impact activities:** Running, jumping, plyometrics (risk of spinal loading)
- **Maintain neutral spine:** No excessive flexion, extension, or rotation
- **Moderate intensity:** Zone 2 (conversational pace) for most sessions; occasional Zone 3 (harder breathing)
- **Progressive duration:** Build capacity gradually; avoid sudden volume increases
- **Low-impact modalities:** Cycling, rowing, swimming, elliptical, walking

## Cardio Modalities & Recommendations

### **Tier 1: Optimal (Low-Impact, Spine-Friendly)**

#### **1. Stationary Cycling (Upright or Recumbent)**

**Why:** Low-impact; neutral spine; adjustable intensity; easy to monitor.

**Setup:**
- Seat height: Knee slightly bent at bottom of pedal stroke
- Handlebar height: Neutral spine; no excessive forward flexion
- Recumbent bike: Preferred for maximum spinal support

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 20–25 minutes, moderate intensity (RPE 5–6/10), 3–4 times per week
- **Weeks 5–8:** 25–30 minutes, moderate intensity (RPE 6–7/10), 2–3 times per week
- **Weeks 9–12:** 30–35 minutes, mixed intensity (see below), 2 times per week

**Intensity Variations:**
- **Steady-state:** Constant moderate pace (Zone 2)
- **Tempo intervals:** 5 min warm-up, 3 × 5 min at RPE 7/10 with 2 min recovery, 5 min cool-down
- **Pyramid:** 5 min warm-up, 2–3–4–3–2 min intervals at RPE 7–8/10 with equal recovery, 5 min cool-down

---

#### **2. Rowing Machine (Concept2 or Similar)**

**Why:** Full-body, low-impact; engages core; excellent for posterior chain.

**Setup:**
- Seat height: Mid-shin when shins vertical
- Footplate: Secure straps; feet flat
- Posture: Neutral spine throughout; drive from legs first, then back, then arms

**Technique Cues:**
- **Drive phase:** Legs extend, torso leans back slightly (not excessively), arms pull
- **Recovery phase:** Arms extend, torso folds forward slightly (controlled, not aggressive), legs bend
- **Avoid:** Excessive spinal flexion or hyperextension; jerky movements

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 15–20 minutes, moderate intensity (RPE 5–6/10), 2 times per week
- **Weeks 5–8:** 20–25 minutes, moderate intensity (RPE 6–7/10), 2 times per week
- **Weeks 9–12:** 25–30 minutes, mixed intensity, 1–2 times per week

**Intensity Variations:**
- **Steady-state:** Constant moderate pace (500 m / 2 min splits)
- **Interval sets:** 5 min warm-up, 5 × 3 min at RPE 7/10 with 2 min recovery, 5 min cool-down
- **Pyramid:** 5 min warm-up, 2–3–4–3–2 min intervals at RPE 7–8/10, 5 min cool-down

---

#### **3. Swimming or Pool Walking**

**Why:** Zero-impact; buoyancy reduces spinal load; full-body engagement; excellent for recovery.

**Modalities:**
- **Freestyle (front crawl):** Neutral spine; rhythmic breathing
- **Backstroke:** Spinal extension; avoid if uncomfortable
- **Breaststroke:** Moderate spinal flexion; acceptable if controlled
- **Pool walking:** Shallow end; water resistance without impact

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 20–25 minutes, easy pace (RPE 4–5/10), 1–2 times per week
- **Weeks 5–8:** 25–30 minutes, moderate pace (RPE 5–6/10), 1–2 times per week
- **Weeks 9–12:** 30–35 minutes, mixed pace, 1 time per week

**Intensity Variations:**
- **Steady-state:** Continuous swimming at comfortable pace
- **Interval sets:** 5 min warm-up, 5 × 2 min hard with 1 min easy, 5 min cool-down
- **Mixed strokes:** Alternate strokes every 100 m to vary stimulus

---

#### **4. Elliptical Machine**

**Why:** Low-impact; adjustable resistance; neutral spine; easy to control intensity.

**Setup:**
- Stride length: Comfortable; no excessive forward lean
- Resistance: Moderate; avoid excessive forward flexion
- Posture: Upright; engage core; neutral spine

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 20–25 minutes, moderate resistance (RPE 5–6/10), 2–3 times per week
- **Weeks 5–8:** 25–30 minutes, moderate resistance (RPE 6–7/10), 2 times per week
- **Weeks 9–12:** 30–35 minutes, mixed resistance, 1–2 times per week

### **Active Recovery Days**

- Maintain strength training at reduced volume (see Phase sections)

### **Monitoring Fatigue**

- **Resting heart rate:** Track morning RHR; increase of 5+ bpm suggests overtraining
- **Heart rate variability (HRV):** If available, monitor; low HRV suggests inadequate recovery
- **Perceived exertion:** Rate overall fatigue 1–10; aim for 6–7/10 on training days
- **Performance:** Declining strength or cardio performance suggests overtraining

## Cardio Modifications for Specific Concerns

### **If Lower Back Pain Emerges During Cardio**

1. **Rowing:** Reduce forward flexion; use shorter stroke; reduce intensity
2. **Cycling:** Adjust seat height and position; reduce resistance; check posture
3. **Swimming:** Avoid backstroke if uncomfortable; stick to freestyle or breaststroke
4. **Elliptical:** Reduce stride length; reduce resistance; check posture
5. **Walking:** Reduce pace; check posture; avoid hills

**Action:** Stop the session; assess; modify or switch modality; consult trainer or physio if pain persists.

### **If Fatigue Accumulates**

1. Reduce cardio frequency to 1 day per week temporarily
2. Reduce cardio duration by 25–50%
3. Reduce cardio intensity (steady-state only; no intervals)
4. Increase sleep by 1 hour
5. Increase caloric intake by 200–300 kcal
6. Increase protein intake by 10–20 g

## Core Principles for Ab Training Post-Disc Herniation

### **What to Avoid**

- **Loaded spinal flexion:** Crunches, sit-ups, weighted crunches, cable crunches
- **Excessive spinal flexion under load:** Heavy ab wheel rollouts from standing, heavy decline sit-ups
- **Rotational stress:** Heavy cable woodchops, medicine ball slams with rotation
- **Hyperextension:** Excessive back extensions, upright ab machines
- **Ballistic movements:** Explosive crunches, plyometric ab work

### **What's Safe**

- **Anti-rotation work:** Pallof presses, Landmine rotations, cable chops (light, controlled)
- **Anti-extension work:** Planks, dead bugs, ab wheel rollouts (kneeling or standing with control)
- **Anti-lateral flexion:** Suitcase carries, side planks, Pallof holds
- **Isometric stability:** Planks, hollow body holds, dead bugs
- **Controlled flexion (minimal load):** Decline sit-ups (bodyweight only, slow tempo), ab wheel (kneeling)
- **Dynamic stability:** Bird dogs, quadruped shoulder taps, dead bugs with movement

---

## Safe Ab Exercises by Category

### **Category 1: Anti-Rotation (Primary Focus)**

These exercises teach the core to resist rotation—critical for spinal stability and disc health.

#### **1. Pallof Press (Cable)**

**Setup:**
- Stand perpendicular to cable machine; cable at chest height
- Feet shoulder-width apart; neutral spine
- Hold handle at chest with both hands; cable creates rotational force

**Execution:**
- Press handle straight forward, resisting rotation
- Hold 1–2 seconds; return to chest
- Repeat all reps on one side, then switch

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 10 each side, light weight (5–10 kg)
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 12 each side, moderate weight (10–15 kg)
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 12–15 each side, moderate weight (15–20 kg)

**Tempo:** 2 seconds press, 1 second hold, 2 seconds return

**Cues:**
- Tall posture; engage glutes
- Press straight forward; resist urge to rotate
- Breathe out on press; in on return

---

#### **2. Pallof Hold (Cable)**

**Setup:**
- Same as Pallof press; cable at chest height
- Hold handle at chest with both hands

**Execution:**
- Hold position, resisting rotation
- Maintain neutral spine; tall posture
- Hold for prescribed time

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 30 sec each side, light weight (5–10 kg)
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 45 sec each side, moderate weight (10–15 kg)
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 60 sec each side, moderate weight (15–20 kg)

**Cues:**
- Brace core; glutes engaged
- Resist rotation; tall posture
- Breathe steadily; don't hold breath

---

#### **3. Landmine Rotation (Anti-Rotation)**

**Setup:**
- Landmine (barbell in corner or landmine attachment)
- Stand perpendicular to landmine; feet shoulder-width apart
- Hold end of barbell at chest with both hands; slight knee bend

**Execution:**
- Rotate torso away from landmine, extending arms slightly
- Return to centre; repeat all reps on one side, then switch
- Resist rotation; control movement

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 10 each side, light load (5–10 kg)
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 12 each side, moderate load (10–15 kg)
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 12–15 each side, moderate load (15–20 kg)

**Tempo:** 2 seconds rotate, 1 second hold, 2 seconds return

**Cues:**
- Rotate from core; keep hips stable
- Neutral spine; no spinal flexion
- Controlled; no momentum

---

#### **4. Cable Chop (Light, Controlled)**

**Setup:**
- Cable machine; cable at high position (above head)
- Stand perpendicular to machine; feet shoulder-width apart
- Hold handle with both hands above opposite shoulder

**Execution:**
- Pull handle diagonally across body toward opposite hip
- Rotate from core; controlled movement
- Return to start; repeat all reps, then switch sides

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 10 each side, light weight (5–10 kg)
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 12 each side, light-moderate weight (10–15 kg)
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 12–15 each side, moderate weight (15–20 kg)

**Tempo:** 2 seconds chop, 1 second hold, 2 seconds return

**Cues:**
- Rotate from core; hips stable
- Controlled; no momentum
- Neutral spine throughout

---

### **Category 2: Anti-Extension (Isometric & Dynamic)**

These exercises teach the core to resist spinal extension—critical for disc health.

#### **1. Plank (Forearm)**

**Setup:**
- Forearms on ground; elbows under shoulders
- Feet together or hip-width apart
- Body in straight line from head to heels

**Execution:**
- Hold position; maintain neutral spine
- Glutes engaged; no sagging hips or piking
- Breathe steadily

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 30–45 sec
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 45–60 sec
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 60–90 sec (or add weight)

**Cues:**
- Glutes squeezed; neutral spine
- No sagging hips; no piking (hips too high)
- Engage core; breathe steadily

**Variations:**
- **Weighted plank:** Add light weight plate on back (5–10 kg)
- **Plank with shoulder taps:** Tap opposite shoulder while holding plank (advanced)

---

#### **2. Dead Bug**

**Setup:**
- Lie on back; arms extended toward ceiling
- Knees bent 90°; hips bent 90°; shins parallel to ground
- Lower back neutral; slight lumbar curve

**Execution:**
- Extend opposite arm and leg simultaneously
- Arm extends overhead; leg extends straight
- Return to start; repeat on other side
- Maintain neutral lumbar spine throughout

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 10 each side, slow tempo
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 12 each side, moderate tempo
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 15 each side, or add light ankle weights (1–2 kg)

**Tempo:** 2 seconds extend, 1 second hold, 2 seconds return

**Cues:**
- Maintain neutral lumbar spine; don't let lower back arch
- Extend fully; controlled return
- Breathe out on extend; in on return

---

#### **3. Ab Wheel Rollout (Kneeling)**

**Setup:**
- Kneel on mat; ab wheel in front
- Hands on wheel handles; shoulders over hips
- Neutral spine; core engaged

**Execution:**
- Roll wheel forward, extending body
- Stop before lumbar spine hyperextends (or when form breaks)
- Roll back to start using core
- Controlled; no momentum

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 6–8 reps, kneeling
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 8–10 reps, kneeling
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 10–12 reps, kneeling (or progress to standing with wall)

**Tempo:** 2 seconds roll out, 1 second hold, 2–3 seconds roll back

**Cues:**
- Maintain neutral spine; don't hyperextend
- Roll from core; controlled eccentric
- Stop before form breaks; quality over range

**Regression:** If too difficult, use wall rollout (roll toward wall; stop before full extension)

**Progression:** Standing rollout against wall (advanced; only if kneeling is easy)

---

#### **4. Hollow Body Hold**

**Setup:**
- Lie on back; arms extended overhead
- Legs extended; slight knee bend
- Lower back neutral; slight lumbar curve

**Execution:**
- Engage core; press lower back into floor
- Hold position; maintain neutral spine
- Breathe steadily

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 20–30 sec
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 30–45 sec
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 45–60 sec

**Cues:**
- Press lower back into floor; engage core
- Neutral spine; no hyperextension
- Breathe steadily; don't hold breath

---

### **Category 3: Anti-Lateral Flexion**

These exercises teach the core to resist side-bending—important for spinal stability.

#### **1. Side Plank (Forearm)**

**Setup:**
- Lie on side; forearm on ground; elbow under shoulder
- Feet stacked or staggered (staggered = easier)
- Body in straight line from head to heels

**Execution:**
- Lift hips off ground; hold position
- Maintain neutral spine; no sagging or piking
- Breathe steadily

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 30–45 sec each side
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 45–60 sec each side
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 60–90 sec each side (or add weight)

**Cues:**
- Hips lifted; neutral spine
- Glutes engaged; no sagging
- Breathe steadily

**Variations:**
- **Side plank with hip dips:** Lower and raise hips (dynamic; 3 × 10 each side)
- **Weighted side plank:** Add light weight plate on hip (5–10 kg)

---

#### **2. Suitcase Carry**

**Setup:**
- Stand upright; hold dumbbell in one hand at side
- Feet shoulder-width apart; neutral spine
- Engage core; tall posture

**Execution:**
- Walk forward, resisting lateral flexion
- Maintain upright posture; don't lean toward weight
- Walk for prescribed distance; switch sides

### **Category 4: Dynamic Stability (Controlled Movement)**

These exercises combine stability with controlled movement.

#### **1. Bird Dog**

**Setup:**
- Quadruped position; hands under shoulders, knees under hips
- Neutral spine; core engaged

**Execution:**
- Extend opposite arm and leg simultaneously
- Arm extends forward; leg extends back
- Return to start; repeat on other side
- Maintain neutral spine throughout

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 10 each side, slow tempo
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 12 each side, moderate tempo
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 15 each side, or add light ankle weights (1–2 kg)

**Cues:**
- Maintain neutral spine; no rotation
- Extend fully; controlled return
- Breathe out on extend; in on return

#### **2. Quadruped Shoulder Tap**

**Setup:**
- Quadruped position; hands under shoulders, knees under hips
- Neutral spine; core engaged

**Execution:**
- Tap opposite shoulder with hand
- Maintain stable hips; no rotation
- Return hand to ground; repeat on other side

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 10 each side, slow tempo
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 12 each side, moderate tempo
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 15 each side

**Tempo:** 1 second tap, 1 second return

**Cues:**
- Maintain neutral spine; no rotation
- Stable hips; no swaying
- Controlled; no momentum

#### **3. Quadruped Hip Circles**

**Setup:**
- Quadruped position; hands under shoulders, knees under hips
- Neutral spine; core engaged

**Execution:**
- Lift one knee slightly off ground
- Draw small circle with knee (clockwise, then counterclockwise)
- Maintain stable torso; no rotation
- Repeat on other side

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 8 circles each direction each side
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 10 circles each direction each side
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 12 circles each direction each side

**Cues:**
- Maintain neutral spine; no rotation
- Stable torso; no swaying
- Small, controlled circles

#### **4. Decline Sit-Up (Bodyweight Only, Slow Tempo)**

**Setup:**
- Decline bench; feet secured
- Hands behind head or across chest
- Neutral spine; slight lumbar curve

**Execution:**
- Slowly curl torso forward, flexing spine minimally
- Stop at 45° (not full sit-up); controlled movement
- Slowly lower back to start
- Minimal spinal flexion; controlled tempo

**Progression:**
- **Weeks 1–4:** 3 × 8–10 reps, hands across chest, slow tempo (3 sec up, 3 sec down)
- **Weeks 5–8:** 3 × 10–12 reps, hands across chest, moderate tempo (2 sec up, 2 sec down)
- **Weeks 9–12:** 3 × 12–15 reps, hands behind head, moderate tempo (2 sec up, 2 sec down)

**Cues:**
- Minimal spinal flexion; stop at 45°
- Slow, controlled movement
- Breathe out on curl; in on lower
- **STOP if any sharp pain in lower back**

### **Overview**

Week 12 is dedicated to testing 1-rep maxes on the three main compound lifts: Back Squat, Barbell Bench Press, and Trap Bar Deadlift. The week is structured to allow adequate recovery between testing sessions and to prioritise form and safety.

### **1RM Testing Protocol**

#### **General Principles**

1. **Warm-up thoroughly:** 10–15 minutes of dynamic mobility + progressive loading
2. **Conservative load progression:** Increase by 5–10 kg per attempt; never jump more than 10 kg
3. **Attempt limit:** Maximum 3–4 attempts per lift; stop if form breaks or pain occurs
4. **Form priority:** Perfect form required; any deviation = no rep
5. **Spotter required:** Have trainer or experienced lifter spot all attempts
6. **Video record:** Record all attempts for form analysis
7. **Stop if pain:** Any sharp or radiating pain in lower back = stop immediately; do not attempt further

### **Why Sleep Matters for This Client**

Sleep is the primary driver of:
- **Muscle protein synthesis:** 70% of growth hormone release occurs during deep sleep
- **Spinal disc recovery:** Intervertebral discs rehydrate during sleep; critical for herniation healing
- **CNS recovery:** Essential for strength adaptation and motor learning
- **Inflammation management:** Sleep deprivation increases systemic inflammation (IL-6, TNF-α, CRP)
- **Hormonal balance:** Testosterone, cortisol, and growth hormone regulation
- **Injury prevention:** Sleep-deprived athletes have 60% higher injury risk
- **Cognitive function:** Decision-making, mood, stress resilience

- Recovery: Predictable sleep enhances adaptation to training stress

## Sleep Hygiene Protocol

### **Sleep Environment Optimization**

#### **1. Darkness**

- **Target:** Complete darkness (0–5 lux)
- **Actions:**
  - Blackout curtains or eye mask
  - Remove LED lights from electronics (clock, charger)
  - Cover windows; eliminate street light
  - Use blackout blinds if necessary

**Why:** Darkness triggers melatonin production; light suppresses it.

---

#### **2. Temperature**

- **Target:** 16–18°C (60–65°F)
- **Actions:**
  - Lower bedroom temperature 1–2 hours before bed
  - Use breathable bedding (cotton, linen)
  - Avoid heavy blankets; use layers for adjustment
  - Ensure good air circulation (fan or open window)

**Why:** Core body temperature drops during sleep; cooler environment facilitates this.

---

#### **3. Noise Control**

- **Target:** <30 dB (quiet bedroom)
- **Actions:**
  - Use earplugs if necessary
  - White noise machine (fan, app) to mask external noise
  - Soundproof curtains if high external noise
  - Silence phone notifications

**Why:** Noise disrupts sleep architecture; consistent sound masks variable noise.

---

#### **4. Bed Quality**

- **Target:** Supportive, comfortable mattress and pillow
- **Actions:**
  - Replace mattress if >7 years old or uncomfortable
  - Use pillow that maintains neutral neck alignment
  - Ensure bed is large enough (no partner disturbance)
  - Wash bedding weekly in cool water

**Why:** Poor sleep surface increases pain and reduces sleep quality.

# Complete 12-Week General Strength Programme with Cardio, Core, Anti-Inflammatory Nutrition, and Recovery
## Client Profile: 42M, Desk Worker, Post-Disc Herniation (L4-L5, Asymptomatic)

---

## Programme Overview

This comprehensive 12-week programme integrates:
- **4 days/week strength training** (lower body squat, upper body push, lower body hinge, upper body pull + core)
- **2 days/week cardio** (low-impact, progressive intensity)
- **2–3 days/week dedicated core work** (anti-rotation, anti-extension, anti-lateral flexion)
- **Anti-inflammatory nutrition** (macronutrient targets, food priorities, meal timing)
- **Sleep & recovery protocol** (8–9 hours, pre-sleep routine, mobility, stress management)
- **1RM testing in Week 12** (structured peaking and testing protocol)

**Weekly Structure:**
- **Monday:** Strength (Lower Squat) + Cardio (Steady-State)
- **Tuesday:** Cardio (Intervals/Tempo)
- **Wednesday:** Strength (Upper Push)
- **Thursday:** Rest or Light Mobility
- **Friday:** Strength (Lower Hinge) + Cardio (Steady-State)
- **Saturday:** Strength (Upper Pull + Core) + Cardio (Intervals/Tempo)
- **Sunday:** Complete Rest

---

# PHASE 1: FOUNDATION (WEEKS 1–4)

## Phase 1 Overview

**Objective:** Establish movement patterns, build baseline strength, assess tolerance, reinforce spinal stability, and develop aerobic base.

**Training Principles:**
- Conservative loads; perfect form priority
- Neutral spine maintained throughout
- RPE 5–6/10 on most exercises
- Moderate volume; adequate recovery
- Consistency and habit-building focus

---

## WEEK 1

### **Monday: Lower Body (Squat-Dominant) + Cardio**

#### **Strength Session (6:00–7:00 AM)**

| Exercise | Sets | Reps | Load | Rest | Notes |
|----------|------|------|------|------|-------|
| **Goblet Squat** | 3 | 10 | 12–16 kg | 90 sec | Weight held at chest; elbows inside knees; neutral spine |
| **Leg Press (machine)** | 3 | 12 | Moderate | 90 sec | Back and head supported; full range without lumbar rounding |
| **Bulgarian Split Squat** | 3 | 8 each | Bodyweight | 90 sec | Rear foot elevated; front knee tracking over toe |
| **Leg Curl (machine)** | 3 | 12 | Moderate | 75 sec | Controlled tempo; 2-second hold at top |
| **Glute Bridge (bodyweight)** | 3 | 15 | Bodyweight | 75 sec | Squeeze glutes hard; neutral spine; no hyperextension |
| **Dead Bug** | 2 | 10 each side | Bodyweight | 60 sec | Slow, controlled; maintain neutral lumbar spine |

**Session Duration:** ~50 minutes

#### **Cardio Session (7:15–7:35 AM)**

| Modality | Duration | Intensity | RPE | Notes |
|----------|----------|-----------|-----|-------|
| **Stationary Cycling** | 20 min | Steady-state | 5–6/10 | Conversational pace; focus on form |

**Total Session Duration:** ~65 minutes

---

#### **Nutrition (Monday)**

**Daily Target:** 2,400–2,600 kcal | 130–140 g protein | 300–350 g carbs | 70–80 g fat

**Sample Meal Plan:**

| Meal | Time | Content | Macros |
|------|------|---------|--------|
| **Breakfast** | 7:00 AM | Oatmeal (50 g) + blueberries (100 g) + walnuts (15 g) + cinnamon + green tea | 400 kcal \| 12 g P \| 55 g C \| 12 g F |
| **Mid-Morning Snack** | 10:00 AM | Greek yoghurt (150 g) + berries (80 g) + almonds (15 g) | 200 kcal \| 18 g P \| 15 g C \| 7 g F |
| **Lunch** | 12:30 PM | Grilled salmon (150 g) + brown rice (150 g cooked) + roasted broccoli (150 g) + olive oil (10 ml) + lemon | 650 kcal \| 40 g P \| 65 g C \| 18 g F |
| **Pre-Workout Snack** | 3:30 PM | Rice cakes (2) + almond butter (20 g) + banana (100 g) | 350 kcal \| 10 g P \| 45 g C \| 12 g F |
| **Post-Workout** | 5:30 PM | Whey protein (30 g) + dextrose (40 g) + water + spinach (50 g) | 250 kcal \| 35 g P \| 40 g C \| 1 g F |
| **Dinner** | 7:00 PM | Lean beef (120 g) + sweet potato (150 g) + mixed salad (150 g) + olive oil (15 ml) + balsamic vinegar | 550 kcal \| 35 g P \| 50 g C \| 18 g F |
| **Evening (Optional)** | 9:00 PM | Dark chocolate (25 g, 70% cacao) + herbal tea | 130 kcal \| 2 g P \| 12 g C \| 8 g F |

**Daily Total:** ~2,530 kcal | 152 g protein | 282 g carbs | 76 g fat

---

#### **Recovery (Monday Evening)**

**Pre-Sleep Routine (10:00 PM Bedtime):**

| Time | Activity | Duration | Purpose |
|------|----------|----------|---------|
| **8:30 PM** | Finish eating/drinking | — | Avoid digestion during sleep |
| **8:45 PM** | Dim lights; reduce blue light | — | Trigger melatonin production |
